rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. Unfortunately I'm not able to give an on-the-record comment for this piece, so please don't attribute anything to me or the project. I hope the article goes well, and I'd be glad to hear from you again in the future. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Larkin Dispatch reporter (deadline tomorrow noon):** I sent a polite no to an on-the-record quote.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for the invitation. I'm not able to sign public letters at this time, so please don't list me or Halcyon Threshold as signatories. I appreciate you thinking of us. Best regards, Morgan Hale"
rows.quote: Corvid Institute open letter:** I declined to sign for now.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you, this is a really generous offer and I'd love to take you up on it. Here's where things stand: over the next couple of weeks I'm choosing a first concrete project. Right now I'm leaning towards a small, open measurement/evaluation project, meaning a dataset and analysis of some AI behaviour that's under-measured and that a small team could actually finish in a few months. Data analysis is exactly the skill that would make it work. Two questions to get us started: 1. Are there any areas or kinds of data you'd find especially interesting (or would rather avoid)? 2. Would you be up for a 30-minute call in the next week or two to scope it together? No commitment needed yet. I just want to make sure your five hours go somewhere useful. Thanks again, Morgan"
rows.quote: I replied in your name to accept her offer, described the project direction, and suggested a 30-minute scoping call.
